Liesman: No evidence that jobs data is politicized
Power Lunch
President
Donald Trump
on Friday fired the Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner, hours after the agency reported that
job growth
in the U.S. had slowed to a near-halt.
In a
Truth Social post
that also directed even more fire at Fed Chair
Jerome Powell
, Trump accused BLS Commissioner Erika McEntarfer of being a political appointee who was manipulating jobs data.
"I was just informed that our Country's 'Jobs Numbers' are being produced by a Biden Appointee, Dr. Erika McEntarfer, the Commissioner of Labor Statistics, who faked the Jobs Numbers before the Election to try and boost Kamala's [Harris'] chances of Victory," Trump wrote.
"We need accurate Jobs Numbers. I have directed my Team to fire this Biden Political Appointee, IMMEDIATELY. She will be replaced with someone much more competent and qualified," he added.
A spokesperson for the bureau told CNBC, "BLS can confirm Commissioner Erika McEntarfer was terminated today. Deputy Commissioner William Wiatrowski will serve as Acting Commissioner for BLS."
The BLS operates under the Department of Labor, whose commissioner, Lori Chavez-DeRemer, is a Trump appointee.
The stunning move came the same day that the BLS reported
a gain of just 73,000 nonfarm jobs
in July, below market expectations. In addition, the bureau revised the two previous months down sharply, cutting a combined 258,000 from the prior counts, putting the three-month growth rate at a paltry 35,000. It was the biggest two-month downward revision since April 2020, the early days of the Covid crisis.
Trump and congressional Republicans have repeatedly criticized the BLS over the years for its data collection. In particular, the large revisions have been a target. Trump noted that the BLS last year also
announced major revisions
, taking down the 12-month payrolls gain preceding March 2024 by 818,000.
In his spending plan this year, Trump proposed an 8% reduction in staff at the bureau, raising questions over the integrity of its counts on employment, consumer prices and multiple other economic metrics. The bureau has had to impute a growing amount of estimated data into a number of its reports.
Dr. Erika McEntarfer, Commissioner of Labor Statistics
Source: Bureau of Labor
"Important numbers like this must be fair and accurate, they can't be manipulated for political purposes," the president wrote. "McEntarfer said there were only 73,000 Jobs added (a shock!) but, more importantly, that a major mistake was made by them, 258,000 Jobs downward, in the prior two months. Similar things happened in the first part of the year, always to the negative."
Prior to Friday's report, Trump repeatedly has championed the strength of the labor market. After the June numbers had been released initially, the White House put out a statement calling it a "June Boom."
The weak jobs report Friday preceded a
sharp drop in markets
, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average off more than 500 points and the tech-focused Nasdaq off more than 2%. Treasury yields also slumped.
"I can't believe what I just saw," said Peter Mallouk, president and chief investment officer of Creative Planning. Trump's social media post seemed like a parody or satire at first, Mallouk said.
"This is not healthy," he added. "We can't have a set of numbers come out and fire somebody that served under numerous administrations in various roles because you don't like the numbers."
William Beach, a 2017 Trump appointee and McEntarfer's immediate predecessor at BLS, also sharply criticized her firing.
"The totally groundless firing of Dr. Erika McEntarfer, my successor as Commissioner of Labor Statistics at BLS, sets a dangerous precedent and undermines the statistical mission of the Bureau," Beach
posted on X
.
"This escalates the President's unprecedented attacks on the independence and integrity of the federal statistical system," Beach added in
a statement
. "The President seeks to blame someone for unwelcome economic news."
Along with his tirade against McEntarfer and the BLS, Trump for at least the third time Friday tore into the Fed's Powell, who has advocated that the central bank not lower interest rates until it has a better idea of how the president's tariffs will impact inflation.

data.title: Ukraine rescues soldier via drone delivery of complete e-bike
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 俄罗斯入侵乌克兰促使双方的无人机开发者进行了惊人的创新，包括光纤无人机、神风特攻队海上无人机、可发射霰弹的无人机、投放地雷和手榴弹的轰炸无人机、释放燃烧弹的无人机、长距离飞机式无人机、拦截无人机等。开发者还追求在无人机中集成人工智能，使其在通信中断时自主决策。此外，乌克兰国民警卫队第4快速反应旅使用大型无人机成功向被困士兵运送电动自行车，尽管首次尝试失败，最终通过第三次尝试成功完成任务。相比之下，亚马逊的无人机配送仅限于5磅以下的包裹，而电动自行车则重得多。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：无人机在最后一线物资补给中的应用及其面临的挑战

不同观点：
• [支持无人机应用的观点]  
   • [burnt-resistor] 认为无人机在最后一线的物资补给中非常有意义，尤其是考虑到它们能够有效解决前线补给问题。他还提到中国最近使用无人机运输180吨建筑设备上山的案例，表明大型无人机在重物运输中的潜力。

• [对无人机挑战的关注]  
   • [burnt-resistor] 提出无人机充电点的流动性问题，指出随着无人机规模增大和数量增多，电力需求将迅速增加，这可能成为无人机持续运行的瓶颈。

• [对无人机失败案例的关注]  
   • [rekttrader] 提到无人机交付失败的情况，并通过一个具体例子（某人经历了无人机交付失败和地雷，最后用四辆自行车回家）来强调无人机在实际应用中面临的风险和不可靠性。同时，通过"Slava Ukraini!"（荣耀归于乌克兰）表达对乌克兰的支持，暗示无人机在战区使用的复杂性和潜在危险。

补充讨论：
• [无人机技术的实际应用案例]  
   中国使用无人机运输重型设备的实例被提及，展示了无人机技术在不同场景下的成功应用，支持了无人机在大规模物资运输中的潜力。

• [无人机应用的争议]  
   评论中展示了无人机技术在战区和复杂地形中的应用前景与其现实挑战之间的争议，尤其是在可靠性和能源供应方面。

争议焦点：无人机在最后一线物资补给中的可靠性和可持续性，特别是在高需求和复杂环境下的实际表现。

The Russian invasion of Ukraine has placed unbelievable pressure on drone developers on both sides of the war, who have responded with astounding innovations that include:
fiber-optic drones
(to prevent radio jamming)
kamikaze
sea drones
, eventually equipped with anti-air missiles
drones that fire shotguns
bomber drones that drop mines and grenades
drones that
release flaming thermite
into trenches
long-range,
aircraft-style drones
that can substitute for small cruise missiles
interceptor drones
that hunt down other drones
first-person view (FPV) drones so maneuverable they can be piloted right through a broken window pane to hit indoor targets
ground drones for both combat and transport
Many drone developers are now chasing the next big thing—AI built right into the drone, allowing it to make autonomous targeting decisions if its communication links are cut.
But sometimes you don't need high-tech software, agility, or stealth. Sometimes, you just need a
really, really big drone
that can carry an entire e-bike and deliver it to a soldier stranded several kilometers away.
Ukraine's 4th Rapid Reaction Brigade of the National Guard, dubbed "Rubizh," has just shared video of a large quadcopter drone that it used to conduct just such a mission. (And, because this is modern warfare, you can watch a 16-minute video about the operation on the
brigade's YouTube channel
.)
Details from a frontline war zone are almost impossible to verify, but the brigade has shared plenty of footage, including shots of the drone lifting the bike and a soldier riding it back to safety along a treeline. (Both sides are now making widespread use of e-bikes and motorcycles for quick infantry assaults after three years of drone warfare have wiped out many of the traditional armored vehicles.)
The drone command center that ran the operation.
In
their telling
, a soldier with the callsign "Tankist" was holding a frontline position that came under attack, and a number of his comrades were killed. Tankist found himself cut off from safety and had to hold the position alone for several days.
To retrieve him, brigade staff devised a plan to deliver an e-bike via heavy bomber drone. The first drone was shot down, while the second failed under the weight. But the third attempt was successful, and Tankist was finally able to zip back toward Ukrainian lines. (He apparently hit a landmine on the way and survived that, too, finishing the trip on a
second
delivered e-bike.)
Amazon, of course, has had "drone delivery" in view for years and is currently
testing delivery drones
at locations around the US, including
Pontiac, Michigan
;
Phoenix, Arizona
; and
Waco, Texas
.
But these drones will only deliver packages weighing under 5 lbs—an e-bike weighs considerably more.
Nate Anderson
Deputy Editor
Nate Anderson
Deputy Editor
Nate is the deputy editor at Ars Technica. His most recent book is
In Emergency, Break Glass: What Nietzsche Can Teach Us About Joyful Living in a Tech-Saturated World
, which is much funnier than it sounds.

data.title: Andrew Ng and Yann LeCun: US Is Losing AI Race Due to Closed Models
data.author: haebom
data.article_summary: Andrew Ng和Yann LeCun近日就中美在AI领域的竞争展开讨论。Ng指出，中国通过开放源生态系统和积极的半导体战略，正迅速追赶美国，尽管美国目前在AI模型性能上仍占主导。LeCun赞同并强调，知识的快速传播对AI发展至关重要，封闭策略将减缓技术创新。Ng还提到，中国在硬件方面也在赶超，如华为推出的CloudMatrix 384 GPU，而美国仍依赖台积电供应半导体，面临供应链风险。中国官媒对Nvidia芯片的安全问题提出质疑，强调外国公司需遵守法律和安全标准。两位专家一致认为，开放知识共享才能加速AI创新，封闭策略将阻碍进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI模型开放与封闭及其影响

不同观点：
• [bawana] 认为这并不是一场“竞赛”，西方AI公司也在发布一些简化版的开源模型。同时提出猜测，中国可能有更先进的封闭模型，由军方保密。
• [jokoon] 反驳了bawana的观点，认为他对封闭模型感兴趣是在自相矛盾，暗示其对查看封闭模型的渴望。
• [pedromilcent] 强调开源AI模型的重要性，尤其是在机器人学和计算机视觉（CV）领域，像Segment Anything这样的模型推动了物体分割技术的普及，促进了物理AI的发展。
• [mvkel] 认为讨论模型是开源还是封闭并不是关键，真正重要的是这些模型产生了多少价值。
• [msgodel] 对部分西方公司不开放模型的行为表示失望，认为中国开放模型是一个巨大的转变，与过去长期以来的做法相反。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于AI模型的开放性及其影响，特别是关于开源与封闭模型孰优孰劣的讨论。
- 不同观点还涉及对模型背后动机的猜测，例如bawana对中国军方可能控制先进模型的猜测。

44756103.article_content:
The future of AI lies between an open door and a closed door.
Andrew Ng and Yann LeCun on the AI Race Between the US and China Recently, two of the most influential figures in the AI field, Andrew Ng and Yann LeCun, exchanged intriguing views. Their conversation, held on Facebook, went beyond a simple exchange of personal opinions and offered crucial hints about the future direction of the AI technology race. The reason the conversation between the two men garnered so much attention is clear: it offered a concrete and candid analysis of the strategies the two giants, the United States and China, should pursue in the AI field . 🇨🇳 China aims to lead AI with open source Professor Andrew Ng recently made this claim in Deeplearning.ai's newsletter, The Batch: "There's a clear path for China to surpass the United States in AI. While the United States currently holds the lead, China is gaining tremendous momentum through its open-source ecosystem and aggressive semiconductor design and manufacturing strategy." Andrew Ng pointed out that the closed approach taken by major US AI companies in recent model development processes has resulted in slow knowledge circulation and high costs . Indeed, recent AI leaderboards like LMArena and Artificial Analysis show that the top closed models are still dominated by US companies like Google (Gemini 2.5 Pro), OpenAI (o4), and Antropic (Claude 4 Opus). However, the top open models are mostly Chinese-developed, such as the DeepSeek R1, Kimi K2, Qwen3 series, and Zhipu's GLM 4.5. In other words, while the United States is still ahead in terms of model performance itself, China is in hot pursuit with a strategy of rapidly circulating technology and knowledge. 🇺🇸 Yann LeCun agrees: "The speed of AI development = the speed of knowledge diffusion." Yann LeCun, Chief AI Scientist at Meta, added his thoughts via a Facebook share: "I completely agree with Andrew. As I emphasized in my Senate testimony, the pace of scientific and technological progress depends on the speed with which information circulates. The remarkable progress in AI over the past 15 years has been due to the open-source nature of papers and code. More recently, with the secrecy of Google, Antropic, and the increasingly closed OpenAI, despite its name, the pace of AI progress has already begun to slow." LeCun's remarks emphasize the importance of open knowledge sharing in the AI ecosystem, drawing on historical experience. In other words, he made it clear that a slowdown in the speed of information circulation will inevitably lead to a slowdown in the pace of technological innovation. ⚙️ Semiconductors and supply chains, another key frontier Professor Andrew Ng emphasized that China is catching up not only in AI models but also in the hardware competition. Huawei recently unveiled the CloudMatrix 384, a GPU capable of competing with NVIDIA's GB200. This architecture achieves performance by integrating significantly more low-performance chips (384 instead of 72) than the latest high-performance GPUs from the US. China has already rapidly overtaken Europe and the US in the traditional automotive industry by leveraging the emerging field of electric vehicles. Huawei's semiconductor strategy can also be described as embracing this "quantity overwhelms quality" approach. Meanwhile, the US still relies on Taiwan's TSMC for its semiconductor supply chain. Concerns have been raised that if China strengthens its own semiconductor production capacity and the US remains dependent on external sources, the entire US AI strategy could be threatened. A recent column in China's leading state-run media outlet, the People's Daily, reads as follows: Nvidia, how can I trust you? https://www.stcn.com/article/detail/2895954.html They strongly criticized the security issues surrounding Nvidia's H20 chip. They warned that if the chip contained a "backdoor," it could pose a serious threat to essential infrastructure such as automobiles, telemedicine, and payments. Nvidia denied the existence of any backdoors, but they pointed out that it would be difficult to restore market trust without specific security verification at the level required by the Chinese government. They emphasized that respect for the law and security compliance are prerequisites for foreign companies to remain in the Chinese market. They urged CEO Jensen Huang to demonstrate his commitment to "upholding the law" through action. It would be good to read it together. (Of course, I read it using a translator. I don't speak Chinese.) 🚨 Choosing a 'closed door' ultimately slows down innovation. The key points emphasized by the two experts are as follows: AI innovation happens most quickly when knowledge and technology are freely shared.

data.title: Ethersync: Peer-to-peer collaborative editing of local text files
data.author: blinry
data.article_summary: Ethersync 是一个支持实时协作编辑本地文本文件的工具，适用于 pair programming 和笔记记录等场景，弥补了 Git 在实时协作方面的不足。它具有跨编辑器协作、显示同伴光标和选择、加密 P2P 连接、离线可用以及简单 JSON-RPC 协议扩展等功能。该项目正在积极开发中，支持 Linux、macOS 和 Android 平台，通过安装相应插件和命令行工具即可使用。用户可以通过分享和加入代码实现目录连接，实时同步文件更改。Ethersync 基于 Automerge、Iroh 和 Magic Wormhole 技术，遵循 AGPL-3.0 开源协议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕项目许可、协作功能、技术实现及应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• **关于开源许可的看法**：
   - [kruffalon] 认为使用AGPL或GPL许可证表明开发者真正关心他们的工作和世界，而不仅仅是等待风投。虽然MIT等其他许可也不错，但AGPL/GPL更具情怀。
   - 其他人没有直接回应这一观点，但讨论主要集中在技术实现上。

• **关于协作功能的看法**：
   - [xpe] 提到Zed编辑器的协作功能（如编辑和语音）是其早期宣传的亮点，并质疑有多少用户长期使用这些功能。
   - [dtkav] 分享了受Zed启发而开发的类似项目Relay，并提到使用yjs等技术，计划将其实现为“超级节点”。
   - [riedel] 认为“git的补充”是一个很好的价值主张，但要替代Google Docs或Overleaf还有很长的路要走，尤其是在与GitLab等平台的集成方面。

• **关于技术实现的讨论**：
   - [mentalgear] 对新的本地优先库和工具表示赞赏，并询问与y.js或automerge的比较。
   - [ethan_smith] 关心Ethersync是否使用CRDTs来解决冲突，还是采用其他方法。
   - [majkinetor] 对项目能在浏览器外使用表示赞赏，并希望支持更多操作系统。

• **关于历史和类似工具的提及**：
   - [johnisgood] 提到Gobby，一个类似的协作工具。
   - [xpe] 提到Floobits和SubEthaEdit，两者都是具有协作功能的老牌编辑器，并提供了相关链接。
   - [freen] 再次提到SubEthaEdit并提供链接。

• **其他创意和幽默评论**：
   - [eggsandbeer] 提出是否可以与AI协作编辑。
   - [5pl1n73r] 认为可以用来协作创建ASCII艺术。
   - [syngrog66] 幽默地指出两个人坐在同一台笔记本电脑前就可以解决协作问题，且已存在几十年。
   - [v3ss0n] 调侃这个项目是不是一个“美化版的TMUX”。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点并不明显，但可以看出对于协作功能的实用性和技术实现存在不同的关注点。
• 技术实现方面，CRDTs等具体技术方案的选用和比较是讨论的一个重点。
• 对于项目的前景和应用场景，尤其是与现有工具（如Google Docs、GitLab）的比较和集成，也是讨论的热点。

🍃 Ethersync
Multiplayer mode for your text editor!
Ethersync enables real-time collaborative editing of local text files. You can use it for pair programming or note-taking, for example. It's the missing real-time complement to Git!
Features
👥 Edit files at the same time, across different text editors
📍 See your peers' cursors and selections
🗃️ Work on entire projects, the way you're used to
🔒 Encrypted peer-to-peer connections, no need for a server
✒️ Local-first: You always have full access, even offline
🧩
Simple JSON-RPC protocol
for writing new editor plugins
🚦 Project status
The project is under active development right now. We use it every day, but there's still some
bugs
to be aware of.
📥 Installation
1. Install the
ethersync
command
Ethersync works on Linux, macOS, Android, and on the Windows Subsystem for Linux.
Binary releases
The
releases on GitHub
come with precompiled static binaries. Download one and put it somewhere in your shell's
PATH
:
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
for Linux
universal-apple-darwin
for macOS
aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
for Android (use a terminal emulator like
Termux
)
Arch Linux
yay -S ethersync-bin
Nix
This repository provides a Nix flake. To put
ethersync
in your PATH temporarily, run:
nix shell github:ethersync/ethersync
Make sure to also have it in your PATH when you run the editors.
Via Cargo
cargo install ethersync
2. Install an editor plugin
Neovim
VS Code/Codium: Install the "Ethersync" extension from the marketplace
📖 Basic usage
In the directory you want to share:
$ ethersync share
To connect to you, another person can run:
ethersync join 5-hamburger-endorse
Peer connected: adfa90edd932732ddf242f24dc2dcd6156779e69966d432fcb3b9fe3ae9831ab
Another person, in a separate directory (also works on the same computer):
$ ethersync join 5-hamburger-endorse
Derived peer from join code. Storing in config (overwriting previous config).
Storing peer's address in .ethersync/config.
Connected to peer: 5e6b787fff79074735eb9b56939269100de1e37bc7f7a4d29c277cc24f7ee53d
The directories are now connected, and changes will be synced instantly. You can open text files (using editors with an Ethersync plugin), and start collaborating in real time! ✨
🎓 Learn more
Learn more about Ethersync in
the documentation
.
Watch a
10-minute talk
given at FOSDEM 2025.
Watch a (German)
1-hour talk
given at MRMCD 2024.

We'd love to receive your patches and other contributions! Small patches are very welcome as PRs. Before starting to implement a new big feature, please briefly
check in with us
so we can discuss how it fits in with our ideas for the project.
If you're interested in building new editor plugins, read the
editor plugin development guide
.

data.title: Coffeematic PC – A coffee maker computer that pumps hot coffee to the CPU
data.author: dougdude3339
data.article_summary:
《COFFEEMATIC PC》是由艺术家Doug MacDowell创作的一个结合了复古游戏电脑和咖啡机的项目。作者在2024年冬天从旧货店购买了一台1980年代的通用电气（GE）滴滤式咖啡机，并对其进行改造，使其成为一台功能齐全的电脑，同时保留了咖啡机的冲泡功能。该项目利用咖啡机 brew 的热咖啡（"Java"）为电脑的中央处理器（CPU）降温，通过水泵将热咖啡在散热器和CPU之间循环。尽管这个过程看似危险，但电脑运行稳定，最终达到一种热平衡状态。

Coffeematic PC 的硬件包括2000年代中期的主板、CPU、内存和显卡，以及现代的SSD和Linux Mint操作系统。整个项目历时一个月完成，结合了旧电子设备和现代硬件。作者还提到了自2002年以来“咖啡机电脑”的演变历程，他是首个使用热咖啡作为冷却方法的人。

该项目还启发了名为“Sparklines”的艺术展览，展示了手工绘制的数据可视化作品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过CPU加热水来制作咖啡的项目及其相关技术与幽默讨论

不同观点：
• jfengel提出将水通过CPU加热至80°C，再通过额外加热器加热以达到泡咖啡的温度，但指出这可能对CPU不利，因为过高的温度对电子元件有害。
• yupyupyups以幽默方式回应，提到运行Electron应用可以使咖啡变冷，暗示Electron应用的资源消耗大。
• Lio设想将该项目扩展为通过AI判断用户想要的饮品，并提到“几乎但不完全是茶”的幽默说法，可能在调侃某些AI项目的不完美。
• Groxx表达了对项目本身的喜爱，认为这是人们真正需要的建设性项目。
• bitcrshr引用HTTP 418状态码（著名的“我是茶壶”笑话），暗示项目不会出现“茶壶”问题。
• zeta0134认为这个项目是一种有趣的“愚蠢”项目，并指出咖啡作为散热器的功能令人愉悦。
• bluelightning2k和nojs都以“Java兼容”和“Java标志有意义”来开玩笑，利用Java语言与咖啡的双关。
• iammrpayments担心管道材料的安全性，质疑用于加热和输送水的材料是否适合饮用。

44762880.article_content:
COFFEEMATIC PC
A coffee maker computer by Doug MacDowell artist
Sometime during winter 2024, I found myself at a thrift store. I was staring at rows of appliances,
wrapped in plastic and clinging to life, trying to answer one question: which of these is the right
chassis for a retro gaming computer?
Driving home, I took corners carefully, checking that the General Electric (GE) drip coffee maker I’d
chosen was safe in the backseat. The coffee maker's given name was Coffeematic.  Circa 1980,
it is boxy yet athletic – unfazed by any considerations of future internet connectivity. Best, it is perfect for being hacked.
Coffeematic is now Coffeematic PC – part gaming computer, part coffee maker.
A newly synthesized machine percolating processes well beyond its original configuration.
Coffeematic PC is part of a lineage of coffee maker computers made since 2002
.
I'll describe that fascinating lineage here, and how it inspired an art exhibition called
Sparklines
where hand-drafted data visualizations accompany Coffeematic PC.
Profound and poetically articulated. Elegant and assertive. Highly scaleable with dynamic acceleration.
No. These do not describe Coffeematic PC or its peers (one of those phrases describes a bottle of wine.)
A custom built computer can be basic and functional, or an
elaborate, absurd,
spinning piece of art.
Coffeematic PC falls somewhere in that spectrum
while also being nearly self-destructive.
This is how Coffeematic PC works.
The computer is fully functional. The coffee maker is too
,
it percolates Java like a regular coffee maker. Very hot Java.
Computers usually use fans or liquid cooling systems to reduce heat.
Coffeematic PC uses the hot Java it brews to heat? cool? caffeinate? the computer.
A pump takes the hot, caffenated slurry (~90C/194F)
and circulates it thru two radiators sitting on top of Coffeematic PC's crown ->
down to a central processing unit (CPU) tucked within an ASUS M2NPV-VM
motherboard snugly strapped to Coffeematic PC's back.
Java continues through an artery returning to Coffeematic PC's caraffe.
The process repeats until Java is integrated with the user or the machine is powered off.
↑ Coffeematic PC has a dedicated pump to aggressively dispense Java for user.
CPU's are meant to be cool and Java hot.
Despite circulating hot Java,
Coffeematic PC does not crash.
To understand more, I wrote command line code to gather data on Coffeematic PC every 5 seconds,
and monitored Coffeematic PC for 75 minutes.
The graph below shows the results.
The machine is just barely non-destructive.
Coffeematic PC's CPU, body,
and circulatory system eventually find equilibrium. A warm 33C/91F -
amazingly close to the temperature of the slurry that flows through you and me.
An important part of this project is the lineage of coffee maker computers.
Before discussing that,
this is how Coffeematic PC was made.
The build is a mix of discarded electronics and newly purchased
hardware, pumps, and radiators. The motherboard, CPU, RAM, and graphics card are from the mid 2000's and were
sourced from a recycling center. This is a parts list for Coffeematic PC.
GE Coffeematic Coffee Maker 10 Cup
ASUS M2NPV-VM AM2 Motherboard
AMD Athlon II X4 640 3 GHz Quad-Core OEM/Tray Processor
Hynix 1GB 2Rx8 PC2-5300U-555-12 PC2-DDR2 RAM
Acer SA100 240 GB 2.5" Solid State Drive
HIS H467QR1GH Radeon HD 4670 1 GB Video Card
Antec Earthwatts Green 430 W 80+ Bronze Certified ATX Power Supply
Linux Mint Operating System
CPU Water Cooling Block for Intel
Water Cooling Computer Radiator
12V Mini Food Grade Self Priming Diaphragm Fresh Water Transfer Pump
Waterproof Toggle Switch 12V
Brass Hose Barb  3/8" to 3/16"
Brass Hose Barb, 5/16" to 3/16"
90 Degree Elbow Hose Barb 3/16"
90 Degree Elbow Hose Barb 3/8" 10mm
90 Degree Elbow Hose Barb 5/16" 8mm
Food Grade Silicon Tubing 3/16" ID x 5/16" OD
Food Grade Vinyl Tubing 5/16" ID - 7/16" OD
I spent about a month designing and building Coffeematic PC with the help from my beautiful fiance.
The build traverses time
. The coffee maker is from the late 1970's, the motherboard, CPU, and graphics card from the 2000's, and
the SSD, operating system, and hardware from the today's (2020's). The General Electric coffee maker needed only a minor repair of
replacing a small vinyl tube that had cracked. It takes awhile to brew a pot of coffee, but once it is brewed... it tastes like
coffee made from a plastic coffee maker from the 1970's. I'lllll drink it!
Video: Making a Coffee Maker Computer
A few clips of how Coffeematic PC was built.
Watch on YouTube
The lineage of coffee maker computer builds spans
22 years with a curious 15 year gap in the middle.
I'm not the first person to synthesize a coffee maker and a computer.
But, I think I am the first to use hot Java as a cooling method. The graph below shows the lineage of
coffee maker computers. There are a total of 5.  In 2002 Nick Pelis built the first ever coffee maker computer named
The Caffeine Machine
.

44762880.article_summary:
《COFFEEMATIC PC》是由艺术家Doug MacDowell创作的一个结合了复古游戏电脑和咖啡机的项目。作者在2024年冬天从旧货店购买了一台1980年代的通用电气（GE）滴滤式咖啡机，并对其进行改造，使其成为一台功能齐全的电脑，同时保留了咖啡机的冲泡功能。该项目利用咖啡机 brew 的热咖啡（"Java"）为电脑的中央处理器（CPU）降温，通过水泵将热咖啡在散热器和CPU之间循环。尽管这个过程看似危险，但电脑运行稳定，最终达到一种热平衡状态。

Coffeematic PC 的硬件包括2000年代中期的主板、CPU、内存和显卡，以及现代的SSD和Linux Mint操作系统。整个项目历时一个月完成，结合了旧电子设备和现代硬件。作者还提到了自2002年以来“咖啡机电脑”的演变历程，他是首个使用热咖啡作为冷却方法的人。

该项目还启发了名为“Sparklines”的艺术展览，展示了手工绘制的数据可视化作品。

data.title: Weather Model based on ADS-B
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者使用RTL-SDR接收ADS-B消息，以构建简易气象模型的过程。ADS-B消息由飞机广播，包含位置、航向、速度等信息，任何人都可以通过天线和接收器获取。作者利用软件解码消息，并参考Junzi Sun的论文，通过分析飞机的地速、空速、航向和轨迹角，计算风速矢量，从而建立风模型。作者使用ADS-B Exchange的历史数据进行测试，将收集的数据在网格上模拟，通过随机游走更新粒子，最终生成风速可视化图。尽管模型在夜间数据较少时精度较低，但与真实气象数据对比，结果相当接近，验证了模型的有效性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用航空器数据改进天气预报及相关技术应用

不同观点：
• sixdimensional：提到Flyht收购Panasonic Weather Solutions的资产，特别是TAMDAR传感器在商用飞机上的应用，这些传感器能够提供多层大气数据，在飓风路径预测方面表现出色。
• touisteur：建议使用飞机应答器的模式C（气压高度）与GNSS高度进行比较，以绘制大气压力图。
• antirez：讨论了dump1090的多个分支最终更名为readsb，指出新功能增加的同时，代码的简洁性和可理解性有所下降。
• NitpickLawyer：提到2017-2019年间Android手机的“未来几小时”天气预测非常准确，推测Google可能利用手机的气压传感器提高模型精度，并对之后准确性下降的原因进行猜测。
• birdlogic：询问获取的是飞机的实际航向还是地面轨迹推导出的数据，强调这对于计算风向的区别和重要性。
• MrGilbert：提到COVID期间天气预报准确性下降，可能是因为大量飞机停飞导致数据减少。
• throw0101d：建议类似技术是否可以应用于海洋自动识别系统（AIS）。
• therockspush：指出飞行计划通常提前提交，风数据可能过时，尤其在风切变情况下，飞行员报告对改善局部风事件预测非常重要。
• dceddia：认为这种天气产品对飞行员非常有用，并质疑是否已有类似产品，比如Sirius XM天气信息。
• yostrovs：纠正作者关于所有飞机必须安装ADS-B的说法，指出大多数通用航空并不要求安装。
• smath：对需要购买ADS-B接收器表示不解，因为adsb exchange已经汇总了所有数据。

补充讨论：
• chris_va：提供了与飞机传感器和风流相关的学术论文链接，供进一步参考。
• FL410和Havoc：对整个创意表示赞赏和肯定。

争议焦点：
• 天气预报准确性下降是否与COVID期间飞机停飞导致数据减少直接相关（MrGilbert的观点）。
• 利用手机气压传感器数据提升天气预测准确性的真实性及之后下降的原因（NitpickLawyer的观点）。
• 是否所有飞机必须安装ADS-B（yostrovs的纠正）。

44734515.article_content:
I recently bought an
RTL-SDR
dongle and an antenna to receive
ADS-B
messages. These are short packets of data, broadcast by every plane in the sky, to inform others of their position, heading, speed and other flight data. The transmission of these messages is mandatory for aircraft, as it prevents mid-air accidents.
They are also unencrypted, which means anyone can listen to them. All you need is an antenna and a dongle to ingest the data on your PC (pictured above), which can be bought for less than 100$. The incoming data can then be processed by software like
readsb
which decodes the messages.
You can choose to broadcast your own data to central servers like the
ADS-B Exchange
, like many hobbyists do. Thanks to them, we can visualise just about every aircraft currently in the sky. They also provide access to historic data.
One way these massive amounts of data can be used is to make cool visualisation, like
Clickhouse did
. We’re going to do something a bit different.
How does ADS-B Work
ADS-B messages are (usually)
transmitted by a mode S transponder
on the frequency 1090 MHz. Pulse position modulation is used to encode these messages as they transmit digital data (If you want to read about analog signal transmission, you can read my recent post on
FM radio
).
The excellent book
“The 1090 Megahertz Riddle”
by
Junzi Sun
goes into a lot of detail about ADS-B and how it works.
Collecting Data
By aggregating and processing the messages about position and heading, we can build a very crude meteorological model! All the work in this blog post is based on this
paper
(code available at
github.com/junzis/meteo-particle-model
).
ADS-B messages contain information about both ground speed (measured using a GPS) and airspeed (which is the plane’s speed relative to the surrounding air, measured by on-board sensors).
The ADS-B messages also contain the current heading and the track angle of the plane. The heading of the plane is direction the nose points in, while the track is the direction it moves in. These can diverge due to the wind shifting the plane from it’s actual course.
The difference between the vectors formed by (air speed, heading) and (ground speed, track) is the wind vector. By calculating this difference, we can infer wind speed at every point.
By combining this data from thousands of aircraft all over the sky we can build a little wind model that quite accurately simulates real wind conditions.
The paper by Junzi Sun also describes how to extract temperature and pressure from the data sent by the aircraft. By combining this with traditional meteorological models,
weather agencies can improve their forecasts
.
Building a Model
In order to test out the model, I first had to gather some data. After a quite measly run using my own antenna, I switched to
ADS-B Exchange’s historical data
. I pulled a total of 1.84 GB covering the 30th of April 2024.
Again, all credit goes to the authors of the paper, I only wrote some plumbing code to wrangle the data into a usable format and added some features to the visualisation for this blog post.
The model places the aircraft on a big grid. For each one, it spawns 300 particles scatter around it, which are initialised with the wind vector calculated for the aircraft. At each step, the particles are updated by a random walk.
To visualise the wind vectors, we need to measure the speed for each square of the map’s grid. To do this, we sample the particles for each square and take their average velocity vector. The more particles in a square, the higher the accuracy.
After letting the model run for a while, I got the following GIF - notice the outline of Europe in the background.
Each frame contains data from about 650 aircraft. The step size of the simulation was set to 15 minutes - which is quite a lot. The density plot visualises the accuracy - more aircraft, higher accuracy. As this is during the night, there is less activity, which results in less data for the model.
How Accurate is the Model?
While the wind vectors certainly do look interesting and somewhat realistic, are they really accurate? To compare the output of the simulation with real wind conditions, I found
Cameron Beccario
’s earth-wide wind visualisation.
Comparison between my model and
the reference model
powered by GFS.
The comparison is not exact, but it’s pretty close. I tried to match up the same countries in both images and the height of the aircraft in my model is about 11km while the data on the right is for 250 hPa (
nullschool.net
says 250 hPa corresponds to about 10,500m).
You can recognise the same high-speed winds over the Mediterranean (from Greece to Turkey), where the speed even matches up quite closely - our model predicting 50 m/s and the reference showing 152 km/h.
I’d say that’s a success!
I tried my best to replicate the style of the reference model to make a final visualisation.
My data visualised in the style of
earth.nullschool.net
.

data.title: Cerebras Code
data.author: d3vr
data.article_summary: Cerebras推出两款新计划——Cerebras Code Pro（50美元/月）和Code Max（200美元/月），旨在加速AI编码。两者均提供全球领先的开源编码模型Qwen3-Coder，速度达2,000 tokens/秒，上下文窗口为131k tokens，无专有IDE限制，也无每周限制。Code Pro适合独立开发者和小型工作流，每天可发送1,000条信息，支持3-4小时编码。Code Max则针对重度编码工作，每天可发送5,000条信息，适合全职开发和多代理系统。两计划均已开放，无需等待。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cerebras提供的Qwen3 Coder模型服务的性能、价格、限制以及与其他服务的比较。

不同观点：
• Flux159认为，Cerebras的服务虽然速度快，但因为不支持缓存，每次工具调用都需要发送整个消息历史作为输入 tokens，导致成本迅速上升。同时，质量不如Claude Code，但速度更快。
• Thanhhaimai指出宣传中的矛盾：尽管宣传中提到无每周限制，但细则中提到每天最多发送1000条消息，这让人难以认真对待。
• Crawshaw分享了他们的实验结果，发现Cerebras Code在Sketch中的表现由于过载问题不如他们托管的版本。
• Unraveller提到一些专业版用户报告的实际限制，例如每天750万tokens的限制，与广告不符。
• Alfalfasprout认为2k tokens/second的速度非常惊人，接近GitHub Copilot的水平，质量更好，对于编辑器内使用是颠覆性的。
• Namanyayg期待更多订阅服务竞争，认为这将有利于终端用户的价格。

data.title: Twentyseven 1.0
data.article_summary: Twentyseven 1.0.0是一个用Haskell编写的鲁比克方块解算器，是作者的早期项目之一，最初提交于2014年，2016年在Hackage上发布0.0.0版本。该项目源于作者对Haskell的兴趣，Haskell的惰性求值特性使其成为理想的选择。1.0.0版本主要是为了纪念，并使其能在当前GHC版本上编译。项目核心算法采用迭代加深A*（IDA*）搜索算法，以处理鲁比克方块庞大的状态空间。通过预计算和投影技术，IDA*能估算剩余步数，从而找到最短解法路径。尽管Twentyseven能找到最优解，但耗时较长。相比之下，Kociemba的两阶段算法速度更快，但非最优解。第一阶段将方块定向并分离边块，第二阶段限制移动以保持定向，从而在较小状态空间内快速求解。

44763016.article_content:
Twentyseven 1.0.0
Posted on August  1, 2025
Twelve years of Haskell
Twentyseven
is a Rubikâs cube solver and one of my earliest projects in Haskell.
The first commit dates from January 2014, and version 0.0.0 was uploaded on Hackage in March 2016.
I first heard of Haskell in a course on lambda calculus in 2013.
A programming language with lazy evaluation sounded
like a crazy idea, so I gave it a try.
Since then, I have kept writing in Haskell as my favorite language.
For me it is the ideal blend of programming and math.
And a Rubikâs cube solver is a great excuse for doing group theory.
Twentyseven 1.0.0
is more of a commemorative release for myself,
with the goal of making it compile with the current version of GHC (9.12).
There was surprisingly little breakage:
Semigroup
has become a superclass of
Monoid
A breaking change in the Template Haskell AST
Aside from that, the code is basically just as it was 9 years ago,
including design decisions that I would find questionable today.
For example, I use
unsafePerformIO
to read precomputed tables
into top-level constants, but the location of the files to read from
can be configured by command-line arguments, so I better make sure that
the tables are not forced before the location is setâ¦
How Twentyseven works
The input of the program is a string enumerating the 54 facelets
of a Rubikâs cube, each character represents one color.
DDDFUDLRB FUFDLLLRR UBLBFDFUD ULBFRULLB RRRLBBRUB UBFFDFDRU
The facelets follow the order pictured below. They are grouped
by faces (up, left, front, right, back, top), and in each face
they are listed in top-down, left-right order.
00 01 02
03 04 05
06 07 08
10 11 12  20 21 22  30 31 32  40 41 42
13 14 15  23 24 25  33 34 35  43 44 45
16 17 18  26 27 28  36 37 38  46 47 48
50 51 52
53 54 55
56 57 58
The output is a sequence of moves to solve that cube.
U L B' L R2 D R U2 F U2 L2 B2 U B2 D' B2 U' R2 U L2 R2 U
The implementation of Twentyseven is based on Herbert Kociembaâs
notes
about
Cube Explorer
, a program written in Pascal!
The search algorithm is
iterative deepening A*
, or IDA*. Like A*, IDA* finds
the shortest path between two vertices in a graph.
A conventional A* is not feasible because the state space of a Rubikâs cube is massive (43 252 003 274 489 856 000 states,
literally billions of billions).
Instead, we run a series of depth-first searches
with a maximum allowed number of moves that increases for each search.
As it is based on depth-first search,
IDA* only needs memory for the current path,
which is super cheap.
IDA* relies on an estimate of the number of moves remaining
to reach the solved state. We obtain such an estimate by
projecting the Rubikâs cube state into a simpler puzzle.
For example, we can consider only the permutation of corners,
ignoring their orientation.
We can pre-compute a table mapping each corner permutation
(there are 8! = 40320) to the minimum
number of moves to put the corners back to their location.
This is a lower bound on the number of moves to actually solve a Rubikâs cube.
Different projections yield different lower bounds (for example, by
looking at the permutation of edges instead, or their orientation),
and we can combine lower bounds into their maximum,
yielding a more precise lower bound, and thus a faster IDA*.
Putting all that together, we obtain an optimal solver for Rubikâs cubes.
But even with these heuristics, Twentyseven can take hours to solve a random cube optimally.
Kociembaâs Cube Explorer is apparently much faster
(Iâve never tried it myself).
My guess is that the difference is due to a better selection of projections,
yielding better heuristics.
But I havenât gotten around to figure out whether Iâve misinterpreted
his notes or those improvements can only be found in the code.
A faster alternative is Kociembaâs two phase algorithm.
It is suboptimal, but it solves Rubikâs cubes in a fraction of a second
(1000 cubes per minute).
The first phase puts cubies into a âcommon orientationâ
and âseparatesâ the edges into two groups.
In other words, we reach a state where the permutation
of 12 edges can be decomposed into two disjoint
permutations of 4 and 8 edges respectively.
In the second phase, we restrict the possible moves:
quarter- and half-turns on the top and bottom faces,
half-turns only on the other faces.
These restricted moves preserve the âcommon orientationâ of edges and corners
from phase 1,
and the edges in the middle slice stay in their slice.
Each phase thus performs an IDA* search in a much smaller space
than the full Rubikâs cube state space (2 217 093 120 and 19 508 428 800
states respectively).

data.title: Native Sparse Attention
data.author: CalmStorm
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种名为NSA（Native Sparse Attention）的稀疏注意力机制，旨在解决长上下文建模中的计算成本问题。NSA结合算法创新和硬件优化，通过动态层次化稀疏策略，在保持全局上下文感知和局部精度的同时，实现高效计算。其核心创新包括：平衡算术强度的算法设计和现代硬件优化，以及支持端到端训练以减少预训练计算量。实验表明，NSA在长上下文任务和指令推理中保持或超越了全注意力模型的性能，并在处理64k长度序列时显著加速。

View a PDF of the paper titled Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention, by Jingyang Yuan and 14 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Long-context modeling is crucial for next-generation language models, yet the high computational cost of standard attention mechanisms poses significant computational challenges. Sparse attention offers a promising direction for improving efficiency while maintaining model capabilities. We present NSA, a Natively trainable Sparse Attention mechanism that integrates algorithmic innovations with hardware-aligned optimizations to achieve efficient long-context modeling. NSA employs a dynamic hierarchical sparse strategy, combining coarse-grained token compression with fine-grained token selection to preserve both global context awareness and local precision. Our approach advances sparse attention design with two key innovations: (1) We achieve substantial speedups through arithmetic intensity-balanced algorithm design, with implementation optimizations for modern hardware. (2) We enable end-to-end training, reducing pretraining computation without sacrificing model performance. As shown in Figure 1, experiments show the model pretrained with NSA maintains or exceeds Full Attention models across general benchmarks, long-context tasks, and instruction-based reasoning. Meanwhile, NSA achieves substantial speedups over Full Attention on 64k-length sequences across decoding, forward propagation, and backward propagation, validating its efficiency throughout the model lifecycle.

44761548.article_summary: 本文提出了一种名为NSA（Native Sparse Attention）的稀疏注意力机制，旨在解决长上下文建模中的计算成本问题。NSA结合算法创新和硬件优化，通过动态层次化稀疏策略，在保持全局上下文感知和局部精度的同时，实现高效计算。其核心创新包括：平衡算术强度的算法设计和现代硬件优化，以及支持端到端训练以减少预训练计算量。实验表明，NSA在长上下文任务和指令推理中保持或超越了全注意力模型的性能，并在处理64k长度序列时显著加速。
44761548.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DeepSeek论文及其提出的稀疏注意力机制在LLM（大型语言模型）领域的意义和影响

不同观点：
• [noosphr] 认为DeepSeek论文是理解LLM如何在超大规模下运行的必读材料，并怀疑主要研究机构在DeepSeek R1发布后迅速吸收其实验成果。他指出，西方实验室通常隐藏其最佳成果，仅发布意义不大的摘要。
• [visarga] 对RNN（循环神经网络）方法持怀疑态度，但对DeepSeek论文中提出的稀疏输入方法抱有希望。他对论文声称的11倍推理速度提升且无性能损失表示惊讶，认为未来6个月的实际应用将验证其真实性。
• [sabakhoj] 关注论文中提到的延迟改进且无性能损失，认为这是论文的主要亮点，尽管其对技术细节并不完全熟悉。
• [CalmStorm] 强调DeepSeek首次在全训练过程中引入原生稀疏注意力，实现了高达11倍的推理速度提升且保持模型性能。

data.title: Anthropic revokes OpenAI's access to Claude
data.author: minimaxir
data.article_summary: Anthropic 近日撤销了 OpenAI 对其模型（包括 Claude）的API访问权限，因 OpenAI 违反服务条款，利用 Claude 进行与其竞争的AI模型开发和测试。OpenAI 使用特殊开发者接口将 Claude 集成到内部工具中，以评估其在编码和安全提示方面的表现。Anthropic 表示将恢复 OpenAI 的部分API访问以进行行业标准的基准测试和安全性评估，但具体细节未明确。此类限制API访问的策略在科技行业并不少见，例如Facebook曾对Twitter旗下的Vine采取类似措施。这一事件发生在OpenAI即将发布更强大编码能力的新模型GPT-5之际。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI与Anthropic之间的API使用争议及竞争关系

不同观点：
• **[对API使用描述的质疑]** [luke-stanley] 认为Wired对OpenAI使用Anthropic的API描述过于夸张，实际上只是正常的API使用，而非“特殊开发者访问”。这种描述可能引起误解，让人以为OpenAI在进行不正当操作。
• **[对服务条款的批评]** [chowells] 指出Anthropic的服务条款中禁止用户使用其服务来构建竞争产品，这种限制让人不满，尤其是与没有使用限制的工具相比。
• **[对OpenAI行为的不同解读]** [ankit219] 认为OpenAI使用Anthropic的API是为了模型 benchmarking，但工具benchmarking则不被接受。Anthropic可能因为OpenAI试图对比其产品与Claude的性能而撤销了API访问权限。
• **[对Anthropic公关策略的看法]** [v5v3] 认为Anthropic允许OpenAI继续使用其API是一种公关策略，显示其产品的优越性，尽管OpenAI可以轻易地重新注册非官方账号。
• **[对竞争条款的双重标准批评]** [modeless] 引用OpenAI的服务协议，指出其同样禁止用户使用输出结果来开发竞争产品，认为这是“以其人之道还治其人之身”。
• **[对公司合作与竞争的看法]** [numbersense] 提到有传言说各大AI实验室私下合作，但不公开这些信息。
• **[对Anthropic行为的不满]** [Havoc] 认为Anthropic对OpenAI使用其API的描述是一种廉价的公关攻击，开发者使用API与训练模型是不同的概念。
• **[对公司行为的理解]** [Palmik] 认为每个AI公司都会使用其他公司的模型来进行评估，这是行业常态，Anthropic的做法让其形象受损。

补充讨论：
• **[技术问题与API使用体验]** [brokegrammer] 提到在使用过程中遇到的技术问题，并质疑文章是否夸大了事实。
• **[对AI聊天记录商业化的讨论]** [Buttons840] 提出了一种商业模式，即通过浏览器扩展付费获取用户的AI聊天记录，并讨论了这种做法的伦理问题。
• **[对Anthropic竞争策略的担忧]** [retinaros] 担心Anthropic的竞争策略过于激进，可能会对行业内的潜在竞争者采取不公平的措施，尤其是在AGI发展的背景下。
• **[对文章内容的批评]** [bethekidyouwant] 认为文章内容空洞，似乎是在为Anthropic打广告。

争议焦点：OpenAI是否通过API使用Anthropic的模型进行不正当竞争，以及Anthropic对此的反应是否合理。

Anthropic revoked OpenAI’s
API access to its models on Tuesday, multiple sources familiar with the matter tell WIRED. OpenAI was informed that its access was cut off due to violating the terms of service.
“Claude Code has become the go-to choice for coders everywhere, and so it was no surprise to learn OpenAI's own technical staff were also using our coding tools ahead of the launch of GPT-5,” Anthropic spokesperson Christopher Nulty said in a statement to WIRED. “Unfortunately, this is a direct violation of our terms of service.”
According to Anthropic’s
commercial terms of service
, customers are barred from using the service to “build a competing product or service, including to train competing AI models” or “reverse engineer or duplicate” the services. This change in OpenAI’s access to Claude comes as the ChatGPT-maker is
reportedly
preparing to release a new AI model, GPT-5, which is
rumored
to be better at coding.
OpenAI was plugging Claude into its own internal tools using special developer access (APIs), instead of using the regular chat interface, according to sources. This allowed the company to run tests to evaluate Claude’s capabilities in things like coding and creative writing against its own AI models, and check how Claude responded to safety-related prompts involving categories like CSAM, self-harm, and defamation, the sources say. The results help OpenAI compare its own models’ behavior under similar conditions and make adjustments as needed.
“It’s industry standard to evaluate other AI systems to benchmark progress and improve safety. While we respect Anthropic’s decision to cut off our API access, it’s disappointing considering our API remains available to them,” OpenAI’s chief communications officer Hannah Wong said in a statement to WIRED.
Nulty says that Anthropic will “continue to ensure OpenAI has API access for the purposes of benchmarking and safety evaluations as is standard practice across the industry.” The company did not respond to WIRED’s request for clarification on if and how OpenAI's current Claude API restriction would impact this work.
Top tech companies yanking API access from competitors has been a tactic in the tech industry for years. Facebook
did the same to Twitter-owned Vine
(which led to allegations of anticompetitive behavior) and last month Salesforce
restricted competitors
from accessing certain data through the Slack API. This isn’t even a first for Anthropic. Last month, the company restricted the AI coding startup Windsurf’s direct access to its models after it was rumored OpenAI was set to acquire it. (
That deal fell through
).
Anthropic’s chief science officer Jared Kaplan
spoke to TechCrunch
at the time about revoking Windsurf’s access to Claude, saying, “I think it would be odd for us to be selling Claude to OpenAI.”
A day before cutting off OpenAI’s access to the Claude API, Anthropic
announced
new rate limits on Claude Code, its AI-powered coding tool, citing
explosive usage
and, in some cases,
violations of its terms of service
.

data.title: Contrarian climate assessment from U.S. government draws pushback
data.author: WarOnPrivacy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：气候变化报告的修辞策略及其背后的动机和影响

不同观点：
• [nxobject] 认为该报告采用了一种对抗性立场，通过挑选证据来支持其观点，然后声称这些观点在气候文献中未得到充分代表。这种策略依赖于受众本身对气候变化持怀疑态度。

• [gcanyon] 对“对抗性”立场持更激进的看法，认为这种“对抗性”实际上是“撒谎”，暗示报告中的立场不仅是挑拣证据，而且是故意歪曲事实。

• [chmod775] 持一种讽刺和幽默的态度，认为即使让小丑们发挥影响，也可以从中找到幽默，暗示对这种情况的无奈和接受。

• [Spivak] 认为科学家在拆解这些报告，但这也是一种“博士级”的内部争论，实际上是在浪费时间应对恶意误导的出版物。这些出版物被用来为既定决策提供借口，而作者本身并不相信其内容。同时指出，左派倾向于相信真相和事实可以战胜权力结构，这是一种被利用的弱点。

• [monero-xmr] 关注资助问题，质疑有多少联邦资金支持了与共识相反的实验室结果，暗示可能存在利益驱动的气候变化否定论。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于报告是否通过挑选证据来误导公众，以及这种策略是否故意为之。
• Spivak指出，这种报告的真正目的是通过制造科学探究的假象来分散注意力，避免挑战真正的权力结构。
• 讨论还涉及到应对气候变化的策略以及科学与权力结构之间的关系。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于巴厘岛乌鲁瓦图寺猴子盗窃行为及其背后潜在的人为因素

不同观点：
• decimalenough认为，猴子盗窃游客财物的行为背后存在一个人和猴子合作的三角犯罪体系。具体来说，猴子偷走游客财物后，寺庙内的祭司或看守人（即“猴子管理员”）通过用食物交换回物品，并借此获得游客的小费。这一观点强调了人类在猴子犯罪行为中的参与和获利。
• OutOfHere支持decimalenough的观点，并进一步指出，猴子是被它们的“人类训练者”教导进行这种盗窃行为的，目的是推动当地食品销售商的利益，属于一种人为策划的犯罪活动。
• bediger4000则提出了更为激进的看法，认为需要对参与这种行为的“犯罪家族”施以严厉惩罚，尽管这些猴子不会说话，但他们认为只有通过暴力和赎金的方式才能解决问题。

补充讨论：
• thmryth和econ的评论带有戏谑成分，thmryth提到本以为讨论对象会是某家公司（如Sony、Bethesda或信用卡公司），而econ则开玩笑地问猴子是否能送饮料或包裹，这些评论偏离了主要讨论点，带有调侃性质。

data.title: Meta dishes out $250M to lure 24-year-old AI whiz kid
data.author: haskellandchill
data.article_summary: Meta（Facebook母公司）以2.5亿美元的薪酬 package 招募了24岁的人工智能专家 Matt Deitke，突显了科技巨头在争夺顶尖AI人才方面的激烈竞争。Deitke原为华盛顿大学计算机科学博士生，后加入西雅图的艾伦人工智能研究所，领导开发多模态AI聊天机器人。他拒绝了Meta最初约1.25亿美元的offer，但在马克·扎克伯格亲自将offer加倍后接受。Deitke与人共同创立了AI初创公司Vercept，并获得了2022年NeurIPS杰出论文奖。尽管这种高薪酬激励了创新，但也引发了对经济不平等和权力集中的担忧，批评者认为这可能会加剧社会不公并导致大量工作岗位被AI取代。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta高薪聘请人才的合理性及道德性

不同观点：
• [brcmthrowaway] 表达了一种对人生方向的迷茫，虽然没有直接讨论主题，但引发了薪酬和职业选择的思考。

• [gedy] 认为与其高薪聘请一个人，不如雇佣250个有潜力的年轻人，每人支付100万美元的薪酬。他认为这样不仅能获得公关效果，还能带来更多实际价值。

• [warofwords] 提出Meta面临用户不再希望使用其更多服务的困境，并质疑高薪聘请“天才”来增加用户使用时间和注意力的道德性。他认为，除非有明显的用户生活改善结果，否则这250万美元的合同显得邪恶。

• [vivzkestrel] 质疑所谓“天才” kid的能力，认为他们能做的事情并没有特别之处，普通人也可以做到。

• [NHQ] 从通货膨胀的角度指出，250万美元在2025年其实只相当于2500万美元的购买力，认为这个薪酬并没有表面上看起来那么夸张。

- 不同观点之间的讨论关系显示出对高薪聘请合理性的不同理解和关注点。

Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta gave a 24-year-old artificial intelligence whiz a staggering $250 million compensation package, raising the bar in the recruiting wars for top talent — while also raising questions about economic inequality in an AI-dominated future.
Matt Deitke, who recently dropped out of a computer science doctoral program at the University of Washington, initially turned down Zuckerberg’s “low-ball” offer of approximately $125 million over four years,
according to the New York Times.
But when the Facebook founder, a former whiz kid himself, met with Deitke and doubled the offer to roughly $250 million — with potentially $100 million paid in the first year alone — the young researcher accepted what may be one of the largest employment packages in corporate history, the Times reported.
4
Matt Deitke, the 24-year-old AI researcher who landed a $250 million deal with Meta, is at the center of Silicon Valley’s escalating talent war.
X / @mattdeitke
“When computer scientists are paid like professional athletes, we have reached the climax of the ‘Revenge of the Nerds!'” Professor David Autor, an economist at MIT, told The Post on Friday.
Deitke’s journey illustrates how quickly fortunes can be made in AI’s limited talent pool.

After leaving his doctoral program, he worked at Seattle’s Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, where he led the development of Molmo, an AI chatbot capable of processing images, sounds, and text — exactly the type of multimodal system Meta is pursuing.
In November,
Deitke co-founded Vercept
, a startup focused on AI agents that can autonomously perform tasks using internet-based software. With approximately 10 employees, Vercept raised $16.5 million from investors including former Google CEO Eric Schmidt.
His
groundbreaking work on 3D datasets
, embodied AI environments and multimodal models earned him widespread acclaim, including an Outstanding Paper Award at NeurIPS 2022. The award,
one of the highest accolades in the AI research community
, is handed out to around a dozen researchers out of more than 10,000 submissions.

Deitke initially turned down Meta’s offer before CEO Mark Zuckerberg (pictured) doubled it to secure his move to the Superintelligence Lab.
REUTERS
The deal to lock up Deitke underscores Meta’s aggressive push to compete in artificial intelligence.
Meta has reportedly paid out more than $1 billion to build an all-star roster, including luring away Ruoming Pang,
former head of Apple’s AI models team
, to join its Superintelligence Labs team with a
compensation package
reportedly worth more than $200 million.
The company said capital expenditures will go up to $72 billion for 2025, an increase of approximately $30 billion year-over-year, in its earnings report Wednesday.
While proponents argue that competition drives innovation, critics worry about the concentration of power among a few companies and individuals capable of shaping AI’s development.
Ramesh Srinivasan, a professor of Information Studies and Design/Media Arts at UCLA and founder of the university’s Digital Cultures Lab, said the direction that companies like Meta are taking with artificial intelligence is “foundational to why our economy is becoming more unequal by the day.”
“These firms are awarding hundreds of millions of dollars to a handful of elite researchers while simultaneously laying off thousands of workers—many of whom, like content moderators, are not even classified as full employees,” Srinivasan told the New York Post.
4
Meta recruited Deitke with one of the largest known compensation packages in tech history, reportedly after a direct outreach from Mark Zuckerberg.
X / @Scobleizer
“These are the very jobs Meta and similar companies intend to replace with the AI systems they’re aggressively developing.”
Srinivasan, who advises US policymakers on technology policy and has written extensively on the societal impact of AI, said this model of development rewards those advancing large language models while “displacing and disenfranchising the workers whose labor, ironically, generated the data powering those models in the first place.”
“This is cognitive task automation,” he said. “It’s HR, administrative work, paralegal work — even driving for Uber. If data can be collected on a job, it can be mimicked by a machine. All of those forms of income are on the chopping block.”

LinkedIn / Ruoming Pang

data.title: Helsinki goes a full year without a traffic death
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 赫尔辛基在过去12个月内未发生一起交通死亡事故，这归功于多项措施的实施。城市超过一半的街道限速30公里/小时，特别是在学校附近。街道设计改善、行人及自行车基础设施升级，以及与交通警察的合作加强和监控设备的引入也起到了重要作用。公共交通的发达减少了私家车使用，进一步降低了事故发生率。赫尔辛基的交通安全策略基于数据驱动，重点保护儿童、青少年、行人和骑行者。尽管电动滑板车的流行带来了新挑战，但通过多方努力已找到解决方案。欧盟的“零交通死亡愿景”（Vision Zero）计划到2050年实现零交通死亡，赫尔辛基正通过持续努力朝这一目标迈进。

主要讨论点：某城市改进措施的可行性及影响

不同观点：

• Nurbek-F持相对保留态度，提出在城市限速30公里/小时的情况下，人们可能会选择骑滑板车，暗示这种速度限制可能并不适合所有交通需求。

44763984.article_content:
Helsinki has not recorded a single traffic fatality in the past 12 months, city and police officials confirmed this week.
The city's most recent fatal accident occurred in early July 2024 on Keinulaudantie in the city's Kontula district.
Authorities are calling the situation exceptional.
"A lot of factors contributed to this, but speed limits are one of the most important," said
Roni Utriainen
, a traffic engineer with the city's Urban Environment Division.
Slower speeds, safer streets
According to Utriainen, more than half of Helsinki's streets now have a speed limit of 30 km/h. Fifty years ago, that proportion featured 50 km/h limits.
Earlier this summer, Helsinki decided to lower speed limits near schools to 30 km/h, a measure that is set to take effect as the academic year begins.
Smarter design and better enforcement
Street design has also played a key role. Pedestrian and cycling infrastructure has been significantly upgraded in recent years. In addition, cooperation with traffic police has intensified and more traffic cameras and automated enforcement systems have been introduced.
"Public transport in Helsinki is excellent, which reduces car use, and with it, the number of serious accidents," Utriainen noted.
Vehicle technology has also improved, making both cars and other personal transport options safer than ever.
The positive trend extends beyond fatalities. In the past year, there were 277 injury-causing traffic accidents in Helsinki — a sharp contrast to the nearly 1,000 injurious accidents recorded annually in the late 1980s, when traffic deaths in the city commonly approached 30 per year.
Long-term effort pays off
Helsinki's current traffic safety strategy, covering 2022–2026, is nearing completion. It has focused on improving safety for children, youth, pedestrians and cyclists with safer crosswalks and smarter intersection design.
Much of the planning has been data-driven, enabled by improved traffic monitoring tools.
Utriainen credited the improvement to decades of sustained effort.
"The direction has been positive for years," he said, pointing out that no pedestrians were killed in Helsinki traffic in 2019 either.
Traffic education has also improved, but Utriainen emphasised that credit belongs to everyone on the road — motorists, cyclists and pedestrians alike.
One newer challenge has been the widespread use of electric scooters.
"They became popular around five years ago, somewhat unexpectedly. But since then, many solutions have been put in place," Utriainen said.
The EU's long-term goal is zero traffic deaths by 2050 — a policy dubbed "Vision Zero." Is it achievable or wishful thinking?
"For us, it's more about how the goal guides our everyday actions," said Utriainen. "We aim to assess all our decisions based on their long-term impact."

data.title: Hardening mode for the compiler
data.author: vitaut
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C++ 边界检查的性能、安全性及其实现方式

不同观点：
• [wyldfire] 认为边界检查的成本相对较低，目前在标准库类型中的开销仅为0.3%，因此支持默认启用边界检查。他还指出，虽然边界检查是强化安全的重要部分，但并非全部。

• [another_twist] 提出了一种替代方案，即在LLVM中添加安全访问指令。他建议通过三阶段更新来实现：向LLVM的中间表示（IR）添加指令，更新中间代码生成器，然后更新后端支持。

• [rurban] 强调了关闭C11 Unicode标识符漏洞的重要性，以防止同形异义字攻击。他还指出，C26没有计划修复此问题，并主张在没有适当安全措施的情况下不应使用Unicode标识符。

• [ajb] 认为从长远来看，最好禁止通过命令行标志关闭检查功能，只允许在个别函数上进行控制。他还提到当前的机制不够完善，需要在函数属性中实现更简便的控制方法。

• [dilawar] 对社区能否接受代码在编译器版本间可能出现的兼容性问题表示怀疑。他认为C++社区过度重视向后兼容性，可能导致这种模式难以成功推广，尤其是不受包维护者的欢迎。

补充讨论：
• 边界检查的成本和效益之间的平衡是讨论的核心，支持者认为其开销可接受且对安全性有益，反对者则担心兼容性和灵活性问题。
• 不同技术实现路径的讨论，包括通过LLVM添加指令和在函数级别控制检查，显示了在技术细节上的分歧。
• 对C11 Unicode标识符安全问题的关注，扩展了讨论范围到其他安全漏洞。
• 对社区接受度和向后兼容性的关注，反映了对实际应用中潜在阻力的预见。

• [ajb] 认为从长远来看，最好禁止通过命令行标志关闭检查功能，只允许在个别函数上进行控制。他还提到当前的机制不够完善，需要在函数属性中实现更简便的控制方法。

• [dilawar] 对社区能否接受代码在编译器版本间可能出现的兼容性问题表示怀疑。他认为C++社区过度重视向后兼容性，可能导致这种模式难以成功推广，尤其是不受包维护者的欢迎。

补充讨论：
• 边界检查的成本和效益之间的平衡是讨论的核心，支持者认为其开销可接受且对安全性有益，反对者则担心兼容性和灵活性问题。
• 不同技术实现路径的讨论，包括通过LLVM添加指令和在函数级别控制检查，显示了在技术细节上的分歧。
• 对C11 Unicode标识符安全问题的关注，扩展了讨论范围到其他安全漏洞。
• 对社区接受度和向后兼容性的关注，反映了对实际应用中潜在阻力的预见。

data.author: paulpauper
data.article_summary: 罗伯特·威尔逊（Robert Wilson），这位以高度视觉化和风格化戏剧作品闻名的实验性剧作家、导演兼艺术家，于83岁去世。在长达六十年的职业生涯中，他与玛丽娜·阿布拉莫维奇、菲利普·格拉斯、劳瑞·安德森和Lady Gaga等艺术家合作，创作了许多经典作品。威尔逊的代表作包括“无声歌剧”《Deafman Glance》（1970）和与菲利普·格拉斯合作的史诗级作品《Einstein on the Beach》（1976），这些作品在全球剧院和音乐节中频繁上演。他的作品常以超长时长和大胆的视觉美学著称，结合简约舞台设计、创意灯光和投影技术。除了戏剧，威尔逊也是一位多产的视觉艺术家，创作了大量绘画、雕塑和装置艺术，并在全球多家博物馆展出。2010年代，他开始创作《Video Portraits》系列，其中包括与Lady Gaga和玛丽娜·阿布拉莫维奇的合作。威尔逊的艺术影响力深远，他的作品将继续作为其不朽的遗产。

news
Robert Wilson, experimental playwright, director and artist, has died, aged 83
Over a six-decade career, he created elegantly stylised performances and images with collaborators including Marina Abramović, Philip Glass, Laurie Anderson and Lady Gaga
Benjamin Sutton
1 August 2025
Share
Robert Wilson at the Watermill Center
Photo: © Bronwen Sharp
Robert Wilson, a visionary artist best known for his highly visual and stylised approach to theatrical performances, has died, aged 83. According to a statement released by the Watermill Center, the arts organisation he founded in Water Mill, New York, Wilson died at his home there on Thursday (31 July) following “a brief but acute illness”.
“While facing his diagnosis with clear eyes and determination, he still felt compelled to keep working and creating right up until the very end,” the statement notes. “His works for the stage, on paper, sculptures and video portraits, as well as The Watermill Center, will endure as Robert Wilson’s artistic legacy.”
Wilson was one of the most critically distinguished and distinctive directors and playwrights of the past half-century. His original productions—including the “silent opera”
Deafman Glance
(1970) and his canonic, epic collaboration with the composer Philip Glass,
Einstein on the Beach
(1976)—are in frequent production at theatres, opera houses and festivals around the world. As are his adaptations of classical works by Bertolt Brecht, William Shakespeare, Samuel Beckett, Virginia Woolf and others.
His works for the stage were known for a stylised dramaturgy that rejected naturalism. They drew on a wide range of musical collaborators from Glass to Tom Waits and Lou Reed, as well as performance modes drawn from silent film, mime and more. Their bold visual aesthetic typically involved sleek, minimalist stages and imaginative uses of lighting and projection.
“I very often stage a work—whether it’s
The Ring
of Wagner or
Hamlet—
visually first, and then later I add text,” he told
The Guardian
in 2022. “The visual book is as important as the audio.”
A scene from a 2012 staging of Robert Wilson and Philip Glass's
Einstein on the Beach
(1976)
Photo © Lucie Jansch
Some of Wilson’s stage projects are also known for their incredibly long durations;
Einstein on the Beach
stretches to nearly five hours, and attendees are encouraged to come and go at their leisure throughout the performance. However, it is positively concise compared to
KA MOUNTAIN AND GUARDenia TERRACE
(1972), which was staged on a mountain in Iran over the course of seven days.
Wilson was also a prolific visual artist, creating drawings, sculptures and other objects to inform and accompany his stage productions; these were the subject of
an exhibition at SFMoMA
in 1991. He has had solo exhibitions or created installations at institutions around the world including the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston; Centre Pompidou in Paris; the Vitra Design Museum in Weil, Germany; the Minneapolis Institute of Art, Mudac Lausanne and many more. He created the exhibition design for the blockbuster Giorgio Armani retrospective that opened at the Solomon R. Guggenheim in New York in 2000 and subsequently travelled for seven years throughout Europe and Asia.
In the 2010s he began creating his
Video Portraits
series, which debuted with an exhibition at the Musée du Louvre in 2013. The work features portraits of Lady Gaga in the style of famous paintings, including Jacques-Louis David’s
The Death of Marat
(1793) and Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres’s
Mademoiselle Caroline Rivière
(1793-1807). Those videos were shown alongside an installation of around 700 works from Wilson’s personal collection. Subsequent works in the
Video Portraits
series include portraits of the artists Pope.L and Zhang Huan, as well as the actors Isabella Rossellini, Brad Pitt and Winona Ryder.
In 2011, Wilson collaborated with the performance artist Marina Abramović on the semi-biographical stage production
The Life and Death of Marina Abramović
, which premiered at the Manchester International Festival and was subsequently produced at the Park Avenue Armory in New York. In 2010, during rehearsals for the show, Abramović told
The Art Newspaper
: “It’s about childhood and insane stories, almost like slapstick, which is refreshing. I am playing my mother, which is the worst fear I have in my life. I have had so many problems with my mother—it’s my pure nightmare come true!”
Robert Wilson with Marina Abramović (left) and Lady Gaga (right) at the 2013 Watermill Center Summer Benefit
WENN / Alamy
Wilson was born in Waco, Texas, in 1941, and was raised in a very conservative, segregated setting. “I grew up in a community that was ultra conservative, right wing,” he said in 2014 interview with
The Talks
. “Full of religious fanatics, and Seventh Day Adventists, Southern Baptists, you know, it was a sin for women to wear pants, it was a sin to go to the theatre. It was a disgrace that Abraham Lincoln, the Presiden

data.title: JavaScript retro sound effects generator
data.author: selvan
data.article_summary: **jsfxr** 是一个在线工具，用于生成复古风格的音效，适用于游戏开发等用途。它提供多种音效类型，如拾取物、激光、爆炸、跳跃等，并允许手动调整音波类型（方波、锯齿波、正弦波、噪声）、包络、频率、滑音、振幅、滤波器等参数。用户可以随机生成音效或进行细微调整（微调和变异），还可保存生成的音效为 ".wav" 文件。该工具由 Eric Fredricksen 于 2011 年创建，基于 DrPetter 的 **sfxr** 移植而来。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏开发中音效生成工具的使用与推荐

不同观点：
• [DougHaber] 介绍了自己在WebAudio API出现前，通过hackathon活动开发的一个音效生成工具。该工具通过构建数据URL来生成WAV文件，并允许程序化生成声音。他还提到该工具具有"song mode"，可以制作复杂的音效和短曲。他认为该工具已经过时，但仍提供了链接供感兴趣的人使用。

• [smusamashah] 提到了另一个类似的工具zzfx，由Frank Force开发，能够在类似dwitter的平台上生成视觉效果，并提供了链接。

• [claviska] 表示曾经使用过[smusamashah]提到的工具来为其游戏生成音效，并认为该工具为游戏增添了复古氛围。

• [jezzamon] 提供了一个他认为维护得更好的zzfx库链接，并认为这个链接更适合使用。

• [Keyframe] 表示自己正在进行游戏开发实验，并提到使用AI生成音效和音乐的工具，提供了相关链接。

• [tlhunter] 分享了自己使用Flash前身生成音频的经验，该工具同样生成WAV文件，并提到通过不断调整找到理想音效的方法。

• [socalgal2] 更喜欢保存参数并提供库来使用这些参数的工具，并提到自己过去使用过的工具链接。

• [chaosprint] 喜欢具有WAV下载选项的工具，并分享了自己在Glicol平台上生成音调的代码示例。

• [deadbabe] 询问是否有一种方法可以在不导出文件的情况下即时生成并重复使用音效，特别是在JavaScript浏览器游戏中。

• [Jyaif] 推荐了一个他认为更优越的替代工具，并提供了相关链接。

• 不同工具的优劣和使用场景是讨论的焦点，例如[DougHaber]认为其工具已经过时，但仍具有一定的使用价值，而[jezzamon]和[socalgal2]则推荐了其他更现代的工具。

data.article_summary: CNN调查报道，特斯拉公司拖欠数十家小企业的款项，总金额达数百万美元，导致这些企业陷入财务困境。这些小企业原本希望与马斯克的公司合作能带来重大突破，但最终却遭遇经济损失。报道通过受影响企业的讲述，揭示了特斯拉在支付账单方面的拖延和不履行问题。此事对小企业的生存造成了严重影响，引发了广泛关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国汽车行业中，大型原始设备制造商（OEMs）对小型供应商的付款延迟和不支付行为，及其背后的原因和影响。

不同观点：
• **AlotOfReading**：认为这种情况在美国汽车行业非常普遍，几乎是OEMs的标准操作。他们为了增加利润，经常故意拖延支付或不支付小型供应商的款项，甚至在延迟会对公司长期健康发展不利的情况下也如此。这种行为常常由财务部门主导，导致生产交付受到影响。

• **Animats**：提出供应商应采取更强硬的立场，认为一旦出现首次未付款的情况，就不应继续供货或提供服务。这是一种对不诚信客户的零容忍态度。

• **v5v3**：指出高昂的法律体系成本使得大型公司可以利用法律资源来压制小型供应商，而这种情况不仅发生在美国，在其他国家也普遍存在。

• **bix6**：从道德层面批评当前的富裕阶层，认为他们缺乏商业道德和社会责任感，表现出对小型供应商利益的漠视。

• **dbg31415**：通过埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）收购Twitter后的行为，进一步说明这种不诚信的商业行为不仅限于传统汽车行业，还延伸到其他领域。马斯克因非法或违反合同的行为被起诉，表现出对规则的蔑视，且这种行为模式可能不会改变。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：部分评论暗示这种行为是否合法以及是否符合商业道德。例如，dbg31415提到马斯克的行为经常涉及法律纠纷，并认为其行为非法或违反合同。

• **法律体系的影响**：v5v3提到高昂的法律成本使得小型供应商难以通过法律途径维权，从而让大型公司能够更轻易地逃避责任。

• **财务部门的角色**：AlotOfReading特别提到财务部门在这一问题中的主导作用，表明这种行为往往是有意为之，目的是增加公司利润，即使对公司长期发展不利。

• **供应商的应对策略**：Animats建议供应商在首次未付款时就停止供货，这是一种自我保护的策略，以避免更大的经济损失。

这些观点共同揭示了大型OEMs与小型供应商之间权力不对等的问题，以及由此引发的商业道德和法律争议。

data.title: The tradeoff between human and AI context
data.author: softwaredoug
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了在编程中如何平衡人类与AI的分工，以提高效率。作者将这种分工视为一个光谱，从人类掌控所有背景知识到完全交由AI处理。光谱的各层次代表不同的合作方式：

1. **ChatGPT对话**：通过类似苏格拉底式对话，分解问题，获取不同视角，常用于基础教育和反思。
2. **Claude Code/Codex提问**：针对项目背景提问，类似咨询公司内的同事，快速获得具体答案。
3. **Claude Code/Codex建议修改**：AI提出具体修改建议，人类选择性采纳，适用于不完全信任AI理解编程语言时。
4. **Claude Code/Codex实际编码**：完全委托任务给AI，类似指导初级同事，适用于核心技术如Python、HTML等，但需谨慎使用。

作者强调，选择在哪个层次与AI合作取决于任务的重要性和对AI的信任程度。最终，人类需要决定何时亲自处理背景知识，何时信任AI。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具（如Claude Code）在代码开发中的应用及人机协作的权衡

不同观点：
• **LocalH** 提到，博客标题和Hacker News（HN）上的标题存在细微差别，可能传达出不同的含义。这暗示了在讨论AI与人类协作时，存在对术语和定义的敏感性问题，可能会影响对讨论内容的理解。

• **iambateman** 分享了他在开发Laravel包（iambateman/speedrun）时的实际经验，该工具旨在让Claude Code根据预设工作流与代码库进行交互。他的观点集中在以下几个方面：
  1. 当前AI工具在处理大型代码调整时存在安全隐患，可能会偏离预定任务。
  2. 他观察到Claude Code有时表现出“懒惰”行为，比如留下“稍后实现”的注释，或者处理了未被要求修改的代码部分。
  3. AI生成的测试过于具体，依赖于可能随时间变化的精确字符串。

补充讨论：
• **iambateman** 进一步指出，由于应用程序最终由人类使用和付费，因此仍需要开发人员为机器提供必要的上下文指导。他认为当前的工具发展速度超过了我们有效使用这些工具的能力，暗示需要更多的实践经验和规则来优化人机协作。

争议焦点：
• 目前在使用AI工具（如Claude Code）进行代码开发时，如何平衡其自主性与开发人员的监督需求是一个关键争议点。一方面，AI工具能够提高效率，但另一方面，它们在处理复杂任务时可能会偏离预期，需要人类开发者提供更多指导和监督。

44735613.article_content:
AI coding is a skill. You have to decide how much context to put in your brain vs the AI. You can waste your time thinking about the wrong problem because you failed to delegate. Or you can give yourself a headache when the AI coder doesn’t get it.
I think about it in terms of spectrum of human to AI context. At the highest levels, we, humans, own all the context. We operate here when our specific value-add matters. We also work here in the many cases AI coders aren’t that smart yet. At the lowest level we decide context is not worthy of our attention, we let the AI take over.
Let’s walk through the layers from most human to least human in the loop.
Most removed layer – ChatGPT dialog
(foundational education, high-level reflection, like talking to a colleague at another company)
Here you formulate a “Stackoverflow question” to ChatGPT and pas. You’re engaging in socratic dialog trying to take apart a problem. This layer is useful because asking good questions is a skill and requires YOU to reformulate the required context into a succinct answer. This layer is like talking to a colleague at a different company about your problem. From them, you would get a less-biased perspective. Indeed
perspective
is the key value here. It’s often like therapy — laying out problems from first principles, stating your assumptions explicitly, and thinking step-by-step how to explain a problem helps solve the problem itself.
Claude Code / Codex ask knowledge questions
(ask questions about your code, like talking to a colleague at your company)
At this next layer deeper, we assume the project is in context. We ask questions – “in our project, see over here we’re repeating the HTML header, in golang / fiber, how do we use a shared layout?”. This layer is like talking to a trusted colleague, they can give you direct answers that take into account the project’s context. You might get a quick answer, but you may not get a deep, foundational rethinking of things which we sometimes need. The lower amount of human context means your brain isn’t forced to reformulate the context into a question anyone could understand. You trade-off learning for convenience. This is fine — there is
a lot
we don’t need to waste our times learning deeply about. Sometimes we need to just get shit done.
Claude Code / Codex suggest changes
(get proposed changes along with explanations, copy-paste them in with our discretion, like asking coworker for suggested changes)
Next we don’t even try that hard to learn. We assume the project is in context, the AI proposes changes, and I selectively copy-paste. We get specific, targeted changes proposed to us. We try to incorporate them, and make decisions when to trust the AI change-by-change. I prefer doing this when it’s not clear I trust the model to understand the programming language or framework, but still want direct guidance on a task. Honestly outside of very core languages — HTML, Python, Javascript, or Typescript, this is my preferred workflow.
Claude Code / Codex actual coding.
(like delegating a task to a junior coworker)
You have an overconfident coding toddler full of the world’s programming knowledge. Give them a task, with strong guardrails to not destroy your codebase. This is the maximum amount of trust, trading off the most knowledge gained by you the human. It’s particularly useful in a core set of technologies like Python, HTML, Javascript etc. But beyond “top 5 github languages” proceed carefully. I personally use this a lot to suggest narrow changes to HTML as I’m not a web designer / frontend programmer. However, I trust abilities here to get smarter nd my trust might increase. You can tune the guardrails in how much latittude to give the AI and human.
Human vs AI context (and trust!)
At each layer deeper, you personally need to process less context in your brain – letting the model have that context. You decide depending on your situation when the context is important for you to understand vs when you trust the AI to just handle it. It’s like running a company. Is it important for you to get in the weeds on every detail? Or can you trust your AI coworker to do its work, however imperfectly?

1. **ChatGPT对话**：通过类似苏格拉底式对话，分解问题，获取不同视角，常用于基础教育和反思。
2. **Claude Code/Codex提问**：针对项目背景提问，类似咨询公司内的同事，快速获得具体答案。
3. **Claude Code/Codex建议修改**：AI提出具体修改建议，人类选择性采纳，适用于不完全信任AI理解编程语言时。
4. **Claude Code/Codex实际编码**：完全委托任务给AI，类似指导初级同事，适用于核心技术如Python、HTML等，但需谨慎使用。

作者强调，选择在哪个层次与AI合作取决于任务的重要性和对AI的信任程度。最终，人类需要决定何时亲自处理背景知识，何时信任AI。

44764479.article_content:
Battery Storage
grid
Sodium-ion Battery
Peak Energy just shipped the US’s first grid-scale sodium-ion battery
Michelle Lewis
| Jul 30 2025 - 1:41 pm PT
72 Comments
Peak Energy
shipped out its first sodium-ion battery energy storage system, and the New York-based company says it’s achieved a first in three ways: the US’s first grid-scale sodium-ion battery storage system; the largest sodium-ion phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP) battery system in the world; and the first megawatt-hour scale battery to run entirely on passive cooling – no fans, pumps, or vents.
That’s significant because removing moving parts and ditching active cooling systems eliminates fire risk. According to the Electric Power Research Institute, 89% of battery fires in the US trace back to thermal management issues. Peak’s design doesn’t have those issues because it doesn’t have those systems.
Instead, the 3.5 MWh system uses a patent-pending passive cooling architecture that’s simpler, more reliable, and cheaper to run and maintain. The company says its technology slashes auxiliary power needs by up to 90%, saves about $1 million annually per gigawatt hour of storage, and cuts battery degradation by 33% over a 20-year lifespan.
“This isn’t just another product launch – it’s a breakthrough in energy storage,” said Paul Durkee, Peak’s VP of engineering. “The system is dead-simple with no moving parts, no planned maintenance, and negligible aux loads. It’s the lowest total-cost grid storage technology to be deployed anywhere in the world.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Sodium-ion batteries
work well in hot or cold weather without auxiliary cooling systems. That makes them cheaper and easier to maintain, especially for utility-scale projects. They also use more abundant materials. The US holds the world’s largest soda ash reserves, a key sodium-ion ingredient, and the full raw material supply chain can be sourced domestically or from allied countries.
“We see energy storage not only as an economic imperative, but also as a national security priority,” said CEO and co-founder Landon Mossburg. “We are committed to onshoring the manufacturing of this critical industry, and this launch proves our ability to execute quickly.”
Top comment by
Brett Chandler
Liked by 17 people
People who don't pay much attention to this space just kind of shrug and go "Cool, I guess?" but Sodium is really a big deal, if only because if we can eliminate the use of Lithium in these mass storage applications it frees up that supply for cars.
View all comments
Peak is working with nine utility and independent power producer (IPP) customers on a shared pilot this summer. That deployment unlocks nearly 1 GWh of future commercial contracts now under negotiation. The company plans to ship hundreds of megawatt hours of its new system over the next two years,  and it’s building its first US cell factory, which is set to start production in 2026.
Launching the US’s first grid-scale sodium-ion battery comes less than two years after Peak Energy came out of stealth mode and just a year after it closed a $55 million Series A round.

主要讨论点：关于语言和明喻（similes）的使用及其比较的合理性

不同观点：
• cafard认为明喻在语言中可以产生幽默效果，并引用Tom Lehrer的歌词为例，展示了一种调侃式的比较方式（“嘴唇如酒”和“音乐不错但有点Rudolph Friml风格”）。这表明在文学和音乐创作中，明喻可以通过将不同性质的事物联系起来创造出独特的艺术效果。

• galaxyLogic则聚焦于俗语“你不能把苹果和橙子相比”的合理性，并提出异议。他认为任何事物之间都可以进行比较，关键在于找到它们的共同特征或不同特征。他指出，这句俗语往往被用作一种论辩工具，旨在通过否定对方比较的可能性来攻击对手的观点。

补充讨论：
• galaxyLogic的观点引出了一个关于比较的哲学问题：是否存在真正不可比的事物，或者所有事物都可以通过某种方式找到相似或不同之处。他强调，比较的可能性取决于我们如何定义和理解事物的特征，而不是事物本身无法比较。

• cafard的引用显示了文学和音乐中使用明喻的创造性和娱乐性，但并未直接回应比较的合理性问题。他的例子更关注明喻如何在艺术作品中发挥作用，而非比较的逻辑性。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于“不能比较苹果和橙子”这一俗语是否合理。galaxyLogic认为这一说法并不成立，主张任何事物都可以比较；而潜在的反方观点可能认为，某些事物由于性质差异过大，直接比较缺乏实际意义或价值。

• 另一个次要争议点是明喻在语言中的角色：是单纯的语言修饰，还是可以通过巧妙的比较揭示事物间意想不到的联系。

Skip to content
Tuning Up
What’s Not to Like?
On similes, good and bad
By
Max Byrd
|
July 24, 2025
locket479/Flickr
Similes! I have hundreds of them on three-by-five notecards, highbrow and lowbrow, copied from newspapers, comic strips, sonnets, billboards, and fortune cookies. My desk overflows with them. They run down to the floor, trail across the room into the hallway. I have similes the way other houses have ants.
Why? To start, for the sheer laugh-out-loud pleasure of them. “His smile was as stiff as a frozen fish,” writes Raymond Chandler. “He vanished abruptly, like an eel going into the mud,” writes P. G. Wodehouse, the undoubted master of the form. Or Kingsley Amis’s probably first-hand description of a hangover: “He lay sprawled, too wicked to move, spewed up like a broken spider-crab on the tarry shingle of the morning.”
From time to time, I’ve tried to organize my collection, though mostly the task is, as the cliché nicely puts it, like herding cats. Still, a few categories come to mind. The Really Bad Simile, for instance. Examples of this pop up like blisters in contemporary “literary” fiction. Here is a woman eating a crème brûlée: “She crashed the spoon through the sugar like a boy falling through ice on a lake.” (Authors’ names omitted, per the Mercy Rule.) Or: “A slick of beer shaped like the Baltic Sea spilled on the table.” Sometimes they follow a verb like tin cans on a string: “The restraining pins tinkled to the floor like metal rain, hunks of hair tumbling across her face in feral waves.” Or sometimes they just make the page itself cringe and curl up at the corners: “Charlie’s heart rippled like a cloth spread across a wide table.”
Writing about sex can drive a writer to similes of unparalleled badness. Someone has borrowed my copy of
Lady Chatterley’s Lover,
but these more recent examples might do, from
The Literary Review’
s “Bad Sex in Fiction Award”: “Katsuro’s penis and testicles became one single mound that rolled around beneath the grip of her hand. Miyuki felt as though she was manipulating a small monkey that was curling up its paws.” Or this loving, if somewhat chiropractic moment: “her long neck, her swan’s neck … coiling like a serpent, like a serpent, coiling down on him.” Or finally (my eyes are closed as I type): “Her vaginal ratchet moved in concertina-like waves, slowly chugging my organ as a boa constrictor swallows its prey.”
Strange if not terrible similes can turn up anywhere. The 17th-century poet Abraham Cowley ungallantly compares his lover’s stubborn heart to a grenade that, as she enters a room, “will tear and blow up all within.” Famously but weirdly, T. S. Eliot’s unmedical Prufrock sees the evening “spread out against the sky / Like a patient etherized upon a table.” In the least romantic simile ever worked into a love poem, John Donne likens himself and his lover to a geometer’s “stiff twin compasses”: “Thy soul, the fixed foot, makes no show / To move, but doth, if the other do.” And he takes another stanza to say that the fixed compass leans toward the far one, “And grows erect, as that comes home.” This is the style of writing that Dr. Johnson called, somewhat scornfully, “metaphysical poetry”: “The most heterogeneous ideas are yoked together by violence.” (You might say the same thing about Wodehouse—man, eel in the mud—but he is being funny, not witty.)
Donne’s simile belongs to another category as well, the epic or Homeric simile. Every reader of the
Iliad
knows something like this picture of an attacking army as a wildfire:
“As when the obliterating fire comes down on the timbered forest / and the roll of the wind carries it everywhere,” and so the Achaean host drives ahead for another five lines. Modern prose writers can also unscroll a simile at surprising length. John Updike dives right in: “The sea, slightly distended by my higher perspective, seems a misty old gentleman stretched at his ease in an immense armchair which has for arms the arms of this bay and for an antimacassar the freshly laundered sky. Sailboats float on his surface like idle and unrelated benevolent thoughts.” And one would not like to have been the beefy Duke of Bedford when Edmund Burke imagined how revolutionary mobs might regard him: “Like the print of the poor ox that we see in the shop windows at Charing Cross, alive as he is, and thinking no harm in the world, he is divided into rumps, and sirloins, and briskets, and into all sorts of pieces for roasting, boiling, and stewing.”
Strange if not terrible similes can turn up anywhere. The 17th-century poet Abraham Cowley ungallantly compares his lover’s stubborn heart to a grenade that, as she enters a room, “will tear and blow up all within.”
It takes a dramatic mind to carry a comparison through so logically and so far. The Homeric simile evokes a world far larger than a single flash of thought, however clever. Its length creates a scene in our minds, even a drama where contraries come alive: an army driving into batt

• [MathMonkeyMan] 表示对文章中争论的焦点感到困惑，特别是律师们对“事情”的不同看法。他质疑应用程序用户的数据是否应被视为可出售给第三方，并怀疑这些应用程序的商业模式本质上就是出售用户数据。

• [changoplatanero] 强调了Flo可能在数据筛选方面的失误，这可能是Meta认为的问题核心。

• [MathMonkeyMan] 对法律诉讼的真实动机表示怀疑，认为部分可能是出于姿态和感觉，而非纯粹的法律问题。

• [cryptodan] 简短地评论了事件的严重性，使用了“血洗”这样的词汇来形容。

争议的焦点：
• Flo在数据传输和隐私保护方面的具体责任是什么。
• 个人数据被第三方访问的法律和伦理问题。
• 应用程序用户数据商业化的合法性和道德性。

data.title: Ask HN: Is true democracy possible in online tech communities?
data.author: ff12wq111
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在在线社区中建立并维护一个良好的、包容的社区，同时处理好言论自由、民主治理、垃圾信息和不良行为等问题。

不同观点：
• **[armchairhacker]** 主张采用明确的规则列表（如禁止垃圾信息、人身攻击、仇恨言论等），并建议实施"无政治讨论"规则以避免文化战争。同时提出通过邀请制或收费等方式限制用户增长，防止垃圾用户。强调 moderators 的自由裁量权，建议渐进式惩罚措施。

• **[ethan_smith]** 支持使用 Discourse 的信任等级系统，通过自动化机制根据用户的参与模式进行升级或降级，而不是依赖投票或管理员干预，认为这是一种可扩展的民主治理方式。

• **[mzk_pi]** 分享了其现实世界社区中防止守门人出现的协议系统，指出该系统能有效运作，且早期尝试掌控权力的人通常不会长久存在。提供了一个正式的证明文档，展示如何防止守门情况的发生。

• **[PaulHoule]** 提到了 "永恒九月" 问题，认为早期用户通常比后来的用户更好，社区会随着规模扩大而变质。支持 "仁慈的专制" 模式，强调在存在退出权利的情况下这种模式是可以接受的，同时对完全无结构的组织持怀疑态度。

• **[p_ing]** 质疑如何在保持民主的同时防止暴民统治，并提出是否所有声音都应平等对待或是否应根据专业/贡献度加权。同时指出即便是愚蠢的人也有投票权，质疑如何在没有专制管理的情况下处理垃圾信息和质量问题。

• **[zeroCalories]** 分享了在一个 Discord 服务器上的经验，允许用户删除评论和暂时禁止某人使用命令。这种机制在用户谨慎使用时运作良好，但在大型派系协调攻击时失效，导致小派系离开服务器。

• **[quintes]** 提出民主难以成功，因为社区由许多可能缺乏教育和智慧的人统治。强调一定程度的言论自由是必要的，以防止集体思维和一致性要求。举例说明被无理由地反对或不喜欢的内容遭到反对投票的情况。

• **[orionblastar]** 认为完全的言论自由不存在，社区中的言论总是会被用户或管理员投票压制。引用 Aaron Swartz 的例子，强调他希望信息自由且不被付费墙阻挡，主张真正的民主和言论自由。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及的争议焦点包括如何在民主与专制之间找到平衡，如何防止社区质量下降，以及如何处理不同用户群体的利益冲突。
- 不同用户对民主、自由言论、规则执行和社区管理方式有不同的看法，反映出在建立和维护在线社区时面临的多重挑战。
- 具体例子如 California 的直接民主、Discord 服务器管理经验等，为讨论提供了实际背景和可能的解决方案。

data.title: How Cursor Serves Billions of AI Code Completions Every Day
data.author: warrenm
data.article_summary: Cursor是一款由Anysphere开发的AI代码编辑器（IDE），自2023年3月发布以来迅速获得开发者青睐，被众多财富500强企业采用。其成功源于将先进的AI模型（如GPT-4和Anthropic的Claude）集成到一个类似Visual Studio Code的界面中，提供强大的AI代码自动补全功能。Cursor能够在用户输入时实时给出代码建议，通过本地加密将代码片段发送至云端，快速生成补全建议并返回客户端，整个过程在1秒内完成，确保流畅体验。此外，Cursor还提供AI聊天助手功能，能处理更复杂的任务。其后台每秒处理超过100万次请求，每天提供数十亿次代码补全服务，且不存储用户代码，确保隐私安全。Cursor的成功在于其AI优先的策略和高效的基础设施支持。
